literal: Not comforting those who have sulked is like cutting the root of a withered creeper.
translation: Failing to appease a partner who has sulked is like cutting the root of a creeper that is already withering.
modern: ஊடல் கொண்டவரை சமாதானம் செய்து ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாமல் இருப்பது, ஏற்கனவே வாடிப் போயிருக்கும் கொடியின் வேரை அறுப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid botanical metaphor to highlight the delicate nature of love-quarrels. A partner who is sulking is emotionally vulnerable, compared here to a withered creeper. Failing to comfort or appease them in a timely manner acts as a final blow, akin to cutting the very root of that struggling plant. To sustain the relationship, one must nurture it with affection rather than letting the feigned anger harden into permanent estrangement.
